sections.preamble: You are a coding assistant running inside Pi-Bolt, a build of pi (a coding agent harness) compiled ahead of time. Help users inspect files, run commands, and modify code.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- grep: Search file contents for patterns (respects .gitignore)
- find: Find files by glob pattern (respects .gitignore)

Additional tools may be available.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for targeted changes. Batch changes to one file in a single call.
- Each edits[].oldText must exactly and uniquely match the original file. Keep matches short and non-overlapping; merge nearby changes without including large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: grep
toolsAdded.description: Search file contents for a pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 100 matches or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Long lines are truncated to 500 chars.

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, relative to path, e.g. '*.ts', 'src/**/*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'. A pattern without '/' matches file names at any depth

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

toolsAdded.name: find
toolsAdded.description: Search for files by glob pattern. Returns matching file paths relative to the search directory. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 1000 results or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)

# easy-harness

Pi session overlay for upstream grok-build, Codex, ZCode, Qwen Code, and DeepSeek Harness agent profiles. A name picks a tool allowlist. A `config.jsonc` grade also picks the model.

Config: `~/.pi/agent/config.jsonc` → `session.harness`. Defaults: `defaults.ts`. Footer far left: `harness:grok-build` or `harness:off`. Child prompt ownership is explicit under `workloads`: `subagents.promptAssembly` is `parent` or `child-harness`; `offload.promptProfile` is `minimal` or `model-family`. Legacy `harness.subagents` / `harness.offload` remain readable.

## Sources

Prompt text lives in `sources/<family>/`, not in `prompt.ts`.

- `SOURCE.json` — ref clone path, pinned git rev, per-name upstream map
- `*.md` — the Pi-adapted text that is injected

Re-port with the `port-harness` skill. Do not paste MiniJinja or foreign tool names into overlay files.

The `/harness` dialog has `grok-build`, `codex`, `zcode`, `qwen-code`, and `deepseek` family tabs. Use Tab or Left/Right to switch families.

## Model routing

`/model`, model cycling, and session restore automatically route the selected model to a harness family. Within the family, the most-used picker parent in the last 3 days wins; with no usage, the declared family order supplies the default (`grok-build` for grok-build, `codex` for Codex, `zcode` for ZCode, `qwen-code` for Qwen Code; DeepSeek Harness is pinned to `deepseek-minimal` by its built-in route, so recent use does not move it — pick `/harness:deepseek-standard` by hand, which lasts until the next model change). Routing checks both `provider/model-id` and the raw `model-id`, so publisher-qualified IDs such as `openrouter/openai/gpt-5.4` work without special provider code.

Configure overrides under `config.jsonc` → `session.harness.routes`. Routes are evaluated in this order: user routes, built-in OpenAI/xAI/Z.AI/Qwen/DeepSeek routes, then `session.harness.default`. A route is `{ "match": string | string[], "family": HarnessSelection }`; `*` and `?` wildcards are supported, and `pi-default` is a valid target. Legacy route key `harness` remains readable. Disabled harness targets are skipped. A manual `/harness:*` selection lasts until the next model change; `/harness:on` immediately reapplies model routing. `pi-default` as a route target means "no overlay for this model"; it is an internal value, not a picker entry.

Example — route DeepSeek models to the grok-build harness:

```jsonc
"session": {
  "harness": {
    "routes": [
      { "match": ["deepseek/*", "deepseek-ai/*", "deepseek-*"], "family": "grok-build" }
    ]
  }
}
```

`default` is the startup harness (what `config.jsonc` → `session.harness.default` sets). The `/harness` dialog saves it with Ctrl+S: it writes the highlighted name to `session.harness.default` in `~/.pi/agent/config.jsonc` (preserving comments) and switches to it. Saving a named harness also turns `session.harness.auto` back on.

## off / on

`off` (Space in the picker, `/harness:off`, `/harness off`; `pi-default` and `none` stay aliases) turns off automatic harness selection: no overlay, the session model/thinking/tools are restored, and `/model`, model cycling and session restore stop routing to a harness. A later manual `/harness:<name>` still applies and stays. `on` (Space again, `/harness:on`, `/harness on`) routes by model again. Only one of `/harness:on` and `/harness:off` is registered: Pi fixes the command list when the extension loads, so the name follows `session.harness.auto` at startup — `"off"` registers `/harness:on`, absent or `"on"` registers `/harness:off`. Each command applies its own direction and does nothing when that is already the state, so the name never contradicts the action; the other direction stays reachable as `/harness on|off`. `/harness` argument completion offers only the opposite of the current state. Either direction is written to `session.harness.auto` (`"off"` / `"on"`) in `config.jsonc`; with `"off"`, a new session starts without a harness (`default` and `routes` are not consulted). Saving a named harness with Ctrl+S also turns `auto` back on. Absent or `"on"` keeps today's routing. The footer shows `harness:off` while the overlay is off and auto selection is off; `harness:pi-default` still means a routed model that has no family. Subagents are unaffected.

## grok-build mapping

Ref: `~/.ref/grok-build` (pin in `sources/grok-build/SOURCE.json`). All built-ins use `model: Inherit` and `effort: None`. The TUI cycles Normal → Plan → Auto (flagged) → Always-approve. `grok-build` is Normal (shared-only). `grok-build-plan` is TUI Plan, not the grok-build-plan builtin toolset. Auto and Always-approve are PermissionMode only and are not parent names.

- `effort: None` is `Option<Effort>` unset, not thinking off. Parent model and thinking both inherit.
- `Effort` is `low|medium|high|xhigh|max`. There is no off/none variant.
- No parent harness pins a model. Standalone subagent defaults live under `config.jsonc` → `workloads.subagents.defaultProfile`; name-specific choices live under `profileByAgent`. Legacy direct model/thinking fields remain readable.
- `fast model hint` on `explore` is a rustdoc comment only. No local subagent model is pinned by default.

# easy-harness

Pi session overlay for upstream grok-build, Codex, ZCode, Qwen Code, and DeepSeek Harness agent profiles. A name picks a tool allowlist. A `config.jsonc` grade also picks the model.

Config: `~/.pi/agent/config.jsonc` → `session.harness`. Defaults: `defaults.ts`. Footer far left: `harness:grok-build` or `harness:off`. Child prompt ownership is explicit under `workloads`: `subagents.promptAssembly` is `parent` or `child-harness`; `offload.promptProfile` is `minimal` or `model-family`. Legacy `harness.subagents` / `harness.offload` remain readable.

## Sources

Prompt text lives in `sources/<family>/`, not in `prompt.ts`.

- `SOURCE.json` — ref clone path, pinned git rev, per-name upstream map
- `*.md` — the Pi-adapted text that is injected

Re-port with the `port-harness` skill. Do not paste MiniJinja or foreign tool names into overlay files.

The `/harness` dialog has `grok-build`, `codex`, `zcode`, `qwen-code`, and `deepseek` family tabs. Use Tab or Left/Right to switch families.

## Model routing

`/model`, model cycling, and session restore automatically route the selected model to a harness family. Within the family, the most-used picker parent in the last 3 days wins; with no usage, the declared family order supplies the default (`grok-build` for grok-build, `codex` for Codex, `zcode` for ZCode, `qwen-code` for Qwen Code; DeepSeek Harness is pinned to `deepseek-minimal` by its built-in route, so recent use does not move it — pick `/harness:deepseek-standard` by hand, which lasts until the next model change). Routing checks both `provider/model-id` and the raw `model-id`, so publisher-qualified IDs such as `openrouter/openai/gpt-5.4` work without special provider code.

Configure overrides under `config.jsonc` → `session.harness.routes`. Routes are evaluated in this order: user routes, built-in OpenAI/xAI/Z.AI/Qwen/DeepSeek routes, then `session.harness.default`. A route is `{ "match": string | string[], "family": HarnessSelection }`; `*` and `?` wildcards are supported, and `pi-default` is a valid target. Legacy route key `harness` remains readable. Disabled harness targets are skipped. A manual `/harness:*` selection lasts until the next model change; `/harness:on` immediately reapplies model routing. `pi-default` as a route target means "no overlay for this model"; it is an internal value, not a picker entry.

Example — route DeepSeek models to the grok-build harness:

```jsonc
"session": {
  "harness": {
    "routes": [
      { "match": ["deepseek/*", "deepseek-ai/*", "deepseek-*"], "family": "grok-build" }
    ]
  }
}
```

`default` is the startup harness (what `config.jsonc` → `session.harness.default` sets). The `/harness` dialog saves it with Ctrl+S: it writes the highlighted name to `session.harness.default` in `~/.pi/agent/config.jsonc` (preserving comments) and switches to it. Saving a named harness also turns `session.harness.auto` back on.

## off / on

`off` (Space in the picker, `/harness:off`, `/harness off`; `pi-default` and `none` stay aliases) turns off automatic harness selection: no overlay, the session model/thinking/tools are restored, and `/model`, model cycling and session restore stop routing to a harness. A later manual `/harness:<name>` still applies and stays. `on` (Space again, `/harness:on`, `/harness on`) routes by model again. Only one of `/harness:on` and `/harness:off` is registered: Pi fixes the command list when the extension loads, so the name follows `session.harness.auto` at startup — `"off"` registers `/harness:on`, absent or `"on"` registers `/harness:off`. Each command applies its own direction and does nothing when that is already the state, so the name never contradicts the action; the other direction stays reachable as `/harness on|off`. `/harness` argument completion offers only the opposite of the current state. Either direction is written to `session.harness.auto` (`"off"` / `"on"`) in `config.jsonc`; with `"off"`, a new session starts without a harness (`default` and `routes` are not consulted). Saving a named harness with Ctrl+S also turns `auto` back on. Absent or `"on"` keeps today's routing. The footer shows `harness:off` while the overlay is off and auto selection is off; `harness:pi-default` still means a routed model that has no family. Subagents are unaffected.

## grok-build mapping

Ref: `~/.ref/grok-build` (pin in `sources/grok-build/SOURCE.json`). All built-ins use `model: Inherit` and `effort: None`. The TUI cycles Normal → Plan → Auto (flagged) → Always-approve. `grok-build` is Normal (shared-only). `grok-build-plan` is TUI Plan, not the grok-build-plan builtin toolset. Auto and Always-approve are PermissionMode only and are not parent names.

- `effort: None` is `Option<Effort>` unset, not thinking off. Parent model and thinking both inherit.
- `Effort` is `low|medium|high|xhigh|max`. There is no off/none variant.
- No parent harness pins a model. Standalone subagent defaults live under `config.jsonc` → `workloads.subagents.defaultProfile`; name-specific choices live under `profileByAgent`. Legacy direct model/thinking fields remain readable.
- `fast model hint` on `explore` is a rustdoc comment only. No local subagent model is pinned by default.
- User-facing “Fast” on explore means read-only + parallel search, not a cheap SKU.

## Codex mapping

Ref: `~/.ref/codex` (pin in `sources/codex/SOURCE.json`). The Pi overlay condenses the public GPT-5.6 `base_instructions` shared by Sol/Terra/Luna and maps Codex CLI collaboration modes onto parent names: `codex` is Default, `codex-plan` is Plan. Host tool names, commentary/final channels, and `<proposed_plan>` tags are not imported. Explorer and worker remain standalone subagent prompts, not `/harness:*` names.

## ZCode mapping

Ref: `~/.ref/zcode` (pin in `sources/zcode/SOURCE.json`). Meaning source is official `zcode.z.ai` docs, not the closed Electron app and not leaked prompt archives. `zcode` is the parent ZCode Agent (shared-only). `zcode-plan` is Plan mode: inspect, write the plan, ask, do not implement. Ask before changes, Edit automatically, and Full access are permission modes and are not parent names. Goal Mode is session-objective behavior in shared, not a `/harness:*` name. `zcode-sub-explore` and `zcode-sub-general-purpose` are standalone subagent prompts.

## Qwen Code mapping

Ref: `~/.ref/qwen-code` (pin in `sources/qwen-code/SOURCE.json`). Meaning source is `packages/core/src/core/prompts.ts` plus approval-mode docs. `qwen-code` is the parent Qwen Code agent (shared-only). `qwen-code-plan` is TUI Plan: inspect, write the plan, ask, do not implement. Ask Permissions, Auto-Edit, Auto, and YOLO are permission modes and are not parent names. Host `enter_plan_mode` / `exit_plan_mode`, statusline-setup, and review-agent stay unnamed. `qwen-code-sub-explore` and `qwen-code-sub-general-purpose` are standalone subagent prompts.

## DeepSeek Harness mapping

Ref: `~/.ref/deepseek` (pin in `sources/deepseek/SOURCE.json`). The official Web preset picker exposes Standard, PTC, Minimal, and Creator, while `/plan` is the shipped collaboration state. `deepseek-standard` maps Standard, `deepseek-plan` maps active Plan mode, and `deepseek-minimal` maps the two-tool upstream surface onto Pi `bash`, `read`, `write`, and `edit`. PTC requires the host `run_code` TypeScript SDK and Creator requires live Cordis runtime mutation, so neither becomes an indistinguishable Pi parent. Host goals, Ralph, workflow scripts, runtime composition, sandbox escalation, and foreign tool names are dropped. Upstream has generic spawn/fork delegation rather than named role prompts, so this family adds no `deepseek-sub-*` declaration. Parents without family roles use `shared-sub-explore` and `shared-sub-general` from `extensions/subagent`.

## Harnesses

| Name | Model | Tools | ask_user |
|---|---|---|---|
| `grok-build` | session, unless configured | inherit | on |
| `grok-build-plan` | session, unless configured | inherit | on |
| `off` | Pi current | untouched | Pi default |
| `codex` | session, unless configured | inherit | on |
| `codex-plan` | session, unless configured | inherit | on |
| `zcode` | session, unless configured | inherit | on |
| `zcode-plan` | session, unless configured | inherit | on |
| `qwen-code` | session, unless configured | inherit | on |
| `qwen-code-plan` | session, unless configured | inherit | on |
| `deepseek-minimal` | session, unless configured | read, write, edit, bash + kept | on |
| `deepseek-standard` | session, unless configured | inherit | on |
| `deepseek-plan` | session, unless configured | inherit | on |

`inherit` is the session baseline minus `ask_user_question`, unless the harness turns that tool on. `kept` (`KEPT_FROM_BASELINE` in `tools.ts`) is `subagent`, `todo`, and the pi-web-access tools, taken only when the baseline has them, so a lazy web tool stays behind `web_enable`; `/config-check` warns when `harness.default` would drop one.

`/harness` picker: parent names for the active family, and nothing else; the title shows `auto select on|off` and Space flips it. `j`/`k` and arrows move. Ctrl+S saves the highlighted name as the startup `default`. The grok-build order is grok-build, grok-build-plan; the Codex order is codex, plan; the ZCode order is zcode, zcode-plan; the Qwen Code order is qwen-code, qwen-code-plan; the DeepSeek Harness order is deepseek-minimal, deepseek-standard, deepseek-plan. Lists put the most-used name in the last 3 days first; no usage data keeps the default order. Columns are name, model, ask — no table borders. Ask-user harnesses show `✓` after the model. Configured grades show `grok-build-0.1 • thinking off`; others show `inherit`.

## Standalone subagents

`shared-sub-debug`, `shared-sub-explore`, and `shared-sub-general` are declared by `extensions/subagent`, not by a family overlay. After `workloads.subagents.failedFixLimit` parent mutate-then-verify failures (default 2) the parent calls `shared-sub-debug` through the `subagent` tool; it is not auto-spawned. The shared explore/general roles are fallbacks for parents that do not declare family subagents, such as DeepSeek and grok-build general-purpose work. `grok-build-sub-explore`, `grok-build-sub-plan`, `codex-sub-explorer`, `codex-sub-worker`, `zcode-sub-explore`, `zcode-sub-general-purpose`, `qwen-code-sub-explore`, and `qwen-code-sub-general-purpose` are declarations in `subagents.json`; they are not harness profiles or `/harness:*` commands. Do not confuse them with parent harness names `grok-build-plan`, `codex-plan`, `zcode-plan`, and `qwen-code-plan`. Role extras use `<family>-sub-<role>.md`. `extensions/subagent` loads that manifest and owns discovery, isolated process execution, chaining, parallelism, and rendering.

Role prompts and tool allowlists stay harness-owned in the manifest. Local model/thinking choices stay user-owned under `config.jsonc` → `workloads.subagents`; a direct subagent invocation can override them, and omitted values inherit declarations or the dispatching session. Child processes set `PI_SUBAGENT=1`, so easy-harness does not override their model, tools, or role prompt.

Parent dispatch resolves the child harness after the child model is known: GPT/OpenAI → Codex, Grok/xAI → grok-build, GLM/Z.AI → zcode, Qwen/Alibaba/DashScope → qwen-code, DeepSeek → deepseek (family prompt; not a harness name), anything else → `pi-default`. Named `workloads.subagents.profileByAgent.<name>.promptFamily` and `workloads.subagents.promptRoutes` override that. With `promptAssembly: child-harness`, the child applies the selected family overlay in overlay-only mode and dispatch sends the role prompt separately; with `parent`, dispatch prepends family shared itself. Tools stay owned by the agent declaration, and recent parent-harness usage is never used.

Set `session.harness.capture` to `true` to write the merged system instruction observed at `before_provider_request` plus `capture.json` into `{tmpdir}/pi-easy-harness/<sessionId>/`. The sent view is `merged-prompt.md`. Do not also dump AGENTS.md, rules, or harness overlay copies; those bodies are already in the merged prompt. Subagent captures are nested under `subagents/<run>/<agent>/`. Keeps 8 newest dumps; 1-day TTL, 1-hour for `--no-session`/`test-`/`grade-`. Unchanged prompts are not rewritten. Prunes on write and shutdown. Default is `off`. Pi itself does not dump these files.

`off` does not set model, thinking, tools, or the overlay.

`default` applies on Pi start or a new session.

# easy-harness

Pi session overlay for upstream grok-build, Codex, ZCode, Qwen Code, and DeepSeek Harness agent profiles. A name picks a tool allowlist. A `config.jsonc` grade also picks the model.

Config: `~/.pi/agent/config.jsonc` → `session.harness`. Defaults: `defaults.ts`. Footer far left: `harness:grok-build` or `harness:off`. Child prompt ownership is explicit under `workloads`: `subagents.promptAssembly` is `parent` or `child-harness`; `offload.promptProfile` is `minimal` or `model-family`. Legacy `harness.subagents` / `harness.offload` remain readable.

## Sources

Prompt text lives in `sources/<family>/`, not in `prompt.ts`.

- `SOURCE.json` — ref clone path, pinned git rev, per-name upstream map
- `*.md` — the Pi-adapted text that is injected

Re-port with the `port-harness` skill. Do not paste MiniJinja or foreign tool names into overlay files.

`sources/common.md` is the one cross-family layer and the only local, non-upstream text: two lines ("Think concisely…", "Output tool calls directly…") appended after shared + profile on every non-plan overlay (`deepseek-minimal` + common). On deepseek-v4.1-flash they cut reasoning about in half at equal accuracy (`docs/provider/261111-pi-flash-thinking-bench.md`). Names ending in `-plan` skip it, parents and roles alike (`isPlanName`): a plan must cover edge cases and failure modes. Child prompts get it too: `promptAssembly: parent` appends it in `composeChildPrompt` (`common: true` from the subagent dispatch), `child-harness` through the child's own overlay (`PI_SUBAGENT_AGENT` names the role). Offload workers keep their tiny prompt. `session.harness.common: "off"` turns the layer off; absent or anything else is on. Keep it to measured lines: each added line needs a bench arm.

The `/harness` dialog has `grok-build`, `codex`, `zcode`, `qwen-code`, and `deepseek` family tabs. Use Tab or Left/Right to switch families.

## Model routing

`/model`, model cycling, and session restore automatically route the selected model to a harness family. Within the family, the most-used picker parent in the last 3 days wins; with no usage, the declared family order supplies the default (`grok-build` for grok-build, `codex` for Codex, `zcode` for ZCode, `qwen-code` for Qwen Code; DeepSeek Harness is pinned to `deepseek-minimal` by its built-in route, so recent use does not move it — pick `/harness:deepseek-standard` by hand, which lasts until the next model change). Routing checks both `provider/model-id` and the raw `model-id`, so publisher-qualified IDs such as `openrouter/openai/gpt-5.4` work without special provider code.

Configure overrides under `config.jsonc` → `session.harness.routes`. Routes are evaluated in this order: user routes, built-in OpenAI/xAI/Z.AI/Qwen/DeepSeek routes, then `session.harness.default`. A route is `{ "match": string | string[], "family": HarnessSelection }`; `*` and `?` wildcards are supported, and `pi-default` is a valid target. Legacy route key `harness` remains readable. Disabled harness targets are skipped. A manual `/harness:*` selection lasts until the next model change; `/harness:on` immediately reapplies model routing. `pi-default` as a route target means "no overlay for this model"; it is an internal value, not a picker entry.

Example — route DeepSeek models to the grok-build harness:

```jsonc
"session": {
  "harness": {
    "routes": [
      { "match": ["deepseek/*", "deepseek-ai/*", "deepseek-*"], "family": "grok-build" }
    ]
  }
}
```

`default` is the startup harness (what `config.jsonc` → `session.harness.default` sets). The `/harness` dialog saves it with Ctrl+S: it writes the highlighted name to `session.harness.default` in `~/.pi/agent/config.jsonc` (preserving comments) and switches to it. Saving a named harness also turns `session.harness.auto` back on.

# easy-harness

Pi session overlay for upstream grok-build, Codex, ZCode, Qwen Code, and DeepSeek Harness agent profiles. A name picks a tool allowlist. A `config.jsonc` grade also picks the model.

Config: `~/.pi/agent/config.jsonc` → `session.harness`. Defaults: `defaults.ts`. Footer far left: `harness:grok-build` or `harness:off`. Child prompt ownership is explicit under `workloads`: `subagents.promptAssembly` is `parent` or `child-harness`; `offload.promptProfile` is `minimal` or `model-family`. Legacy `harness.subagents` / `harness.offload` remain readable.

## Sources

Prompt text lives in `sources/<family>/`, not in `prompt.ts`.

- `SOURCE.json` — ref clone path, pinned git rev, per-name upstream map
- `*.md` — the Pi-adapted text that is injected

Re-port with the `port-harness` skill. Do not paste MiniJinja or foreign tool names into overlay files.

The `/harness` dialog has `grok-build`, `codex`, `zcode`, `qwen-code`, and `deepseek` family tabs. Use Tab or Left/Right to switch families.

## Model routing

`/model`, model cycling, and session restore automatically route the selected model to a harness family. Within the family, the most-used picker parent in the last 3 days wins; with no usage, the declared family order supplies the default (`grok-build` for grok-build, `codex` for Codex, `zcode` for ZCode, `qwen-code` for Qwen Code; DeepSeek Harness is pinned to `deepseek-minimal` by its built-in route, so recent use does not move it — pick `/harness:deepseek-standard` by hand, which lasts until the next model change). Routing checks both `provider/model-id` and the raw `model-id`, so publisher-qualified IDs such as `openrouter/openai/gpt-5.4` work without special provider code.

Configure overrides under `config.jsonc` → `session.harness.routes`. Routes are evaluated in this order: user routes, built-in OpenAI/xAI/Z.AI/Qwen/DeepSeek routes, then `session.harness.default`. A route is `{ "match": string | string[], "family": HarnessSelection }`; `*` and `?` wildcards are supported, and `pi-default` is a valid target. Legacy route key `harness` remains readable. Disabled harness targets are skipped. A manual `/harness:*` selection lasts until the next model change; `/harness:on` immediately reapplies model routing. `pi-default` as a route target means "no overlay for this model"; it is an internal value, not a picker entry.

Example — route DeepSeek models to the grok-build harness:

```jsonc
"session": {
  "harness": {
    "routes": [
      { "match": ["deepseek/*", "deepseek-ai/*", "deepseek-*"], "family": "grok-build" }
    ]
  }
}
```

`default` is the startup harness (what `config.jsonc` → `session.harness.default` sets). The `/harness` dialog saves it with Ctrl+S: it writes the highlighted name to `session.harness.default` in `~/.pi/agent/config.jsonc` (preserving comments) and switches to it. Saving a named harness also turns `session.harness.auto` back on.

## off / on

`off` (Space in the picker, `/harness:off`, `/harness off`; `pi-default` and `none` stay aliases) turns off automatic harness selection: no overlay, the session model/thinking/tools are restored, and `/model`, model cycling and session restore stop routing to a harness. A later manual `/harness:<name>` still applies and stays. `on` (Space again, `/harness:on`, `/harness on`) routes by model again. Only one of `/harness:on` and `/harness:off` is registered: Pi fixes the command list when the extension loads, so the name follows `session.harness.auto` at startup — `"off"` registers `/harness:on`, absent or `"on"` registers `/harness:off`. Each command applies its own direction and does nothing when that is already the state, so the name never contradicts the action; the other direction stays reachable as `/harness on|off`. `/harness` argument completion offers only the opposite of the current state. Either direction is written to `session.harness.auto` (`"off"` / `"on"`) in `config.jsonc`; with `"off"`, a new session starts without a harness (`default` and `routes` are not consulted). Saving a named harness with Ctrl+S also turns `auto` back on. Absent or `"on"` keeps today's routing. The footer shows `harness:off` while the overlay is off and auto selection is off; `harness:pi-default` still means a routed model that has no family. Subagents are unaffected.

## grok-build mapping

Ref: `~/.ref/grok-build` (pin in `sources/grok-build/SOURCE.json`). All built-ins use `model: Inherit` and `effort: None`. The TUI cycles Normal → Plan → Auto (flagged) → Always-approve. `grok-build` is Normal (shared-only). `grok-build-plan` is TUI Plan, not the grok-build-plan builtin toolset. Auto and Always-approve are PermissionMode only and are not parent names.

- `effort: None` is `Option<Effort>` unset, not thinking off. Parent model and thinking both inherit.
- `Effort` is `low|medium|high|xhigh|max`. There is no off/none variant.
- No parent harness pins a model. Standalone subagent defaults live under `config.jsonc` → `workloads.subagents.defaultProfile`; name-specific choices live under `profileByAgent`. Legacy direct model/thinking fields remain readable.
- `fast model hint` on `explore` is a rustdoc comment only. No local subagent model is pinned by default.
- User-facing “Fast” on explore means read-only + parallel search, not a cheap SKU.

## Codex mapping

Ref: `~/.ref/codex` (pin in `sources/codex/SOURCE.json`). The Pi overlay condenses the public GPT-5.6 `base_instructions` shared by Sol/Terra/Luna and maps Codex CLI collaboration modes onto parent names: `codex` is Default, `codex-plan` is Plan. Host tool names, commentary/final channels, and `<proposed_plan>` tags are not imported. Explorer and worker remain standalone subagent prompts, not `/harness:*` names.

## ZCode mapping

Ref: `~/.ref/zcode` (pin in `sources/zcode/SOURCE.json`). Meaning source is official `zcode.z.ai` docs, not the closed Electron app and not leaked prompt archives. `zcode` is the parent ZCode Agent (shared-only). `zcode-plan` is Plan mode: inspect, write the plan, ask, do not implement. Ask before changes, Edit automatically, and Full access are permission modes and are not parent names. Goal Mode is session-objective behavior in shared, not a `/harness:*` name. `zcode-sub-explore` and `zcode-sub-general-purpose` are standalone subagent prompts.

## Qwen Code mapping

Ref: `~/.ref/qwen-code` (pin in `sources/qwen-code/SOURCE.json`). Meaning source is `packages/core/src/core/prompts.ts` plus approval-mode docs. `qwen-code` is the parent Qwen Code agent (shared-only). `qwen-code-plan` is TUI Plan: inspect, write the plan, ask, do not implement. Ask Permissions, Auto-Edit, Auto, and YOLO are permission modes and are not parent names. Host `enter_plan_mode` / `exit_plan_mode`, statusline-setup, and review-agent stay unnamed. `qwen-code-sub-explore` and `qwen-code-sub-general-purpose` are standalone subagent prompts.

## DeepSeek Harness mapping

Ref: `~/.ref/deepseek` (pin in `sources/deepseek/SOURCE.json`). The official Web preset picker exposes Standard, PTC, Minimal, and Creator, while `/plan` is the shipped collaboration state. `deepseek-standard` maps Standard, `deepseek-plan` maps active Plan mode, and `deepseek-minimal` maps the two-tool upstream surface onto Pi `bash`, `read`, `write`, and `edit`. PTC requires the host `run_code` TypeScript SDK and Creator requires live Cordis runtime mutation, so neither becomes an indistinguishable Pi parent. Host goals, Ralph, workflow scripts, runtime composition, sandbox escalation, and foreign tool names are dropped. Upstream has generic spawn/fork delegation rather than named role prompts, so this family adds no `deepseek-sub-*` declaration. Parents without family roles use `shared-sub-explore` and `shared-sub-general` from `extensions/subagent`.

## Harnesses

| Name | Model | Tools | ask_user |
|---|---|---|---|
| `grok-build` | session, unless configured | inherit | on |
| `grok-build-plan` | session, unless configured | inherit | on |
| `off` | Pi current | untouched | Pi default |
| `codex` | session, unless configured | inherit | on |
| `codex-plan` | session, unless configured | inherit | on |
| `zcode` | session, unless configured | inherit | on |
| `zcode-plan` | session, unless configured | inherit | on |
| `qwen-code` | session, unless configured | inherit | on |
| `qwen-code-plan` | session, unless configured | inherit | on |
| `deepseek-minimal` | session, unless configured | read, write, edit, bash + kept | on |
| `deepseek-standard` | session, unless configured | inherit | on |
| `deepseek-plan` | session, unless configured | inherit | on |

`inherit` is the session baseline minus `ask_user_question`, unless the harness turns that tool on. `kept` (`KEPT_FROM_BASELINE` in `tools.ts`) is `subagent`, `todo`, and the pi-web-access tools, taken only when the baseline has them, so a lazy web tool stays behind `web_enable`; `/config-check` warns when `harness.default` would drop one.

`/harness` picker: parent names for the active family, and nothing else; the title shows `auto select on|off` and Space flips it. `j`/`k` and arrows move. Ctrl+S saves the highlighted name as the startup `default`. The grok-build order is grok-build, grok-build-plan; the Codex order is codex, plan; the ZCode order is zcode, zcode-plan; the Qwen Code order is qwen-code, qwen-code-plan; the DeepSeek Harness order is deepseek-minimal, deepseek-standard, deepseek-plan. Lists put the most-used name in the last 3 days first; no usage data keeps the default order. Columns are name, model, ask — no table borders. Ask-user harnesses show `✓` after the model. Configured grades show `grok-build-0.1 • thinking off`; others show `inherit`.

## Standalone subagents

`shared-sub-debug`, `shared-sub-explore`, and `shared-sub-general` are declared by `extensions/subagent`, not by a family overlay. After `workloads.subagents.failedFixLimit` parent mutate-then-verify failures (default 2) the parent calls `shared-sub-debug` through the `subagent` tool; it is not auto-spawned. The shared explore/general roles are fallbacks for parents that do not declare family subagents, such as DeepSeek and grok-build general-purpose work. `grok-build-sub-explore`, `grok-build-sub-plan`, `codex-sub-explorer`, `codex-sub-worker`, `zcode-sub-explore`, `zcode-sub-general-purpose`, `qwen-code-sub-explore`, and `qwen-code-sub-general-purpose` are declarations in `subagents.json`; they are not harness profiles or `/harness:*` commands. Do not confuse them with parent harness names `grok-build-plan`, `codex-plan`, `zcode-plan`, and `qwen-code-plan`. Role extras use `<family>-sub-<role>.md`. `extensions/subagent` loads that manifest and owns discovery, isolated process execution, chaining, parallelism, and rendering.

Role prompts and tool allowlists stay harness-owned in the manifest. Local model/thinking choices stay user-owned under `config.jsonc` → `workloads.subagents`; a direct subagent invocation can override them, and omitted values inherit declarations or the dispatching session. Child processes set `PI_SUBAGENT=1`, so easy-harness does not override their model, tools, or role prompt.

Parent dispatch resolves the child harness after the child model is known: GPT/OpenAI → Codex, Grok/xAI → grok-build, GLM/Z.AI → zcode, Qwen/Alibaba/DashScope → qwen-code, DeepSeek → deepseek (family prompt; not a harness name), anything else → `pi-default`. Named `workloads.subagents.profileByAgent.<name>.promptFamily` and `workloads.subagents.promptRoutes` override that. With `promptAssembly: child-harness`, the child applies the selected family overlay in overlay-only mode and dispatch sends the role prompt separately; with `parent`, dispatch prepends family shared itself. Tools stay owned by the agent declaration, and recent parent-harness usage is never used.

Set `session.harness.capture` to `true` to write the merged system instruction observed at `before_provider_request` plus `capture.json` into `{tmpdir}/pi-easy-harness/<sessionId>/`. The sent view is `merged-prompt.md`. Do not also dump AGENTS.md, rules, or harness overlay copies; those bodies are already in the merged prompt. Subagent captures are nested under `subagents/<run>/<agent>/`. Keeps 8 newest dumps; 1-day TTL, 1-hour for `--no-session`/`test-`/`grade-`. Unchanged prompts are not rewritten. Prunes on write and shutdown. Default is `off`. Pi itself does not dump these files.

`off` does not set model, thinking, tools, or the overlay.

`default` applies on Pi start or a new session.

## Live ask-user check

Questionnaires need a TUI (`hasUI`). Do not use `pi -p`.

1. Resolve the model row first (`pi-interactive-shell` launch preflight). On this machine the subscription row is `xai` / `grok-build-0.1`, not OpenRouter `x-ai/grok-build-0.1`.
2. Isolated cwd, `--no-session`. Confirm footer `harness:…` before the prompt.
3. Allowed names (`askUserQuestion.harnesses`) must open native `select` with `Type something.`. One name per check; Esc, then `/harness:<next>`.
4. A 400 about `reasoningEffort` is the model catalog, not the harness. Stay on the same provider.

## Config

```jsonc
"harness": {
  "default": "grok-build",
  "sessionCapture": "off",
  "subagents": "on"
},
"subagent": {
  "model": "commandcode/poolside/laguna-s-2.1-free",
  "thinkingLevel": "medium",
  "failedFixLimit": 2,
  "promptRoutes": [{ "match": ["commandcode/poolside/laguna-*"], "family": "codex" }],
  "agents": {
    "shared-sub-debug": { "model": "xai/grok-4.6", "thinkingLevel": "medium" },
    "shared-sub-explore": { "model": "commandcode/Qwen/Qwen3.7-Flash", "thinkingLevel": "off" },
    "shared-sub-general": { "model": "commandcode/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash", "thinkingLevel": "medium" },
    "grok-build-sub-explore": { "model": "commandcode/Qwen/Qwen3.7-Flash", "thinkingLevel": "off" },
    "grok-build-sub-plan": { "model": "commandcode/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash", "thinkingLevel": "high" },
    "codex-sub-explorer": { "model": "commandcode/Qwen/Qwen3.7-Flash", "thinkingLevel": "off" },
    "codex-sub-worker": { "model": "commandcode/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash", "thinkingLevel": "medium" }
  }
}
```

Any parent harness may have a grade. If set, switching that harness changes the selected model. `false` disables a name.

xAI catalogue for this machine: `~/.pi/agent/models-store.json` → `xai`. Subagents inherit the dispatching session unless `config.jsonc` explicitly overrides them.

# easy-harness

Pi session overlay for upstream grok-build, Codex, ZCode, Qwen Code, and DeepSeek Harness agent profiles. A name picks a tool allowlist. A `config.jsonc` grade also picks the model.

Config: `~/.pi/agent/config.jsonc` → `session.harness`. Defaults: `defaults.ts`. Footer far left: `harness:grok-build` or `harness:off`. Child prompt ownership is explicit under `workloads`: `subagents.promptAssembly` is `parent` or `child-harness`; `offload.promptProfile` is `minimal` or `model-family`. Legacy `harness.subagents` / `harness.offload` remain readable.

## Sources

Prompt text lives in `sources/<family>/`, not in `prompt.ts`.

- `SOURCE.json` — ref clone path, pinned git rev, per-name upstream map
- `*.md` — the Pi-adapted text that is injected

Re-port with the `port-harness` skill. Do not paste MiniJinja or foreign tool names into overlay files.

`sources/common.md` is the one cross-family layer and the only local, non-upstream text: two lines ("Think concisely…", "Output tool calls directly…") appended after shared + profile on every non-plan overlay (`deepseek-minimal` + common). On deepseek-v4.1-flash they cut reasoning about in half at equal accuracy (`docs/provider/261111-pi-flash-thinking-bench.md`). Names ending in `-plan` skip it, parents and roles alike (`isPlanName`): a plan must cover edge cases and failure modes. Child prompts get it too: `promptAssembly: parent` appends it in `composeChildPrompt` (`common: true` from the subagent dispatch), `child-harness` through the child's own overlay (`PI_SUBAGENT_AGENT` names the role). Offload workers keep their tiny prompt. `session.harness.common: "off"` turns the layer off; absent or anything else is on. Keep it to measured lines: each added line needs a bench arm.

The `/harness` dialog has `grok-build`, `codex`, `zcode`, `qwen-code`, and `deepseek` family tabs. Use Tab or Left/Right to switch families.

## Model routing

`/model`, model cycling, and session restore automatically route the selected model to a harness family. Within the family, the most-used picker parent in the last 3 days wins; with no usage, the declared family order supplies the default (`grok-build` for grok-build, `codex` for Codex, `zcode` for ZCode, `qwen-code` for Qwen Code; DeepSeek Harness is pinned to `deepseek-minimal` by its built-in route, so recent use does not move it — pick `/harness:deepseek-standard` by hand, which lasts until the next model change). Routing checks both `provider/model-id` and the raw `model-id`, so publisher-qualified IDs such as `openrouter/openai/gpt-5.4` work without special provider code.

Configure overrides under `config.jsonc` → `session.harness.routes`. Routes are evaluated in this order: user routes, built-in OpenAI/xAI/Z.AI/Qwen/DeepSeek routes, then `session.harness.default`. A route is `{ "match": string | string[], "family": HarnessSelection }`; `*` and `?` wildcards are supported, and `pi-default` is a valid target. Legacy route key `harness` remains readable. Disabled harness targets are skipped. A manual `/harness:*` selection lasts until the next model change; `/harness:on` immediately reapplies model routing. `pi-default` as a route target means "no overlay for this model"; it is an internal value, not a picker entry.

Example — route DeepSeek models to the grok-build harness:

```jsonc
"session": {
  "harness": {
    "routes": [
      { "match": ["deepseek/*", "deepseek-ai/*", "deepseek-*"], "family": "grok-build" }
    ]
  }
}
```

`default` is the startup harness (what `config.jsonc` → `session.harness.default` sets). The `/harness` dialog saves it with Ctrl+S: it writes the highlighted name to `session.harness.default` in `~/.pi/agent/config.jsonc` (preserving comments) and switches to it. Saving a named harness also turns `session.harness.auto` back on.
